subject.title: github-copilot: legacy OAuth token refresh sends bearer credential to unvalidated enterpriseUrl domain

question: Should legacy GitHub Copilot OAuth credentials with non-allowlisted `enterpriseUrl` values fail closed at refresh time, be normalized to `github.com`, or be repaired/scrubbed by doctor before runtime refresh?
rationale: The credential-egress source path is clear, but changing already-persisted legacy auth behavior is both a security-boundary and upgrade-compatibility decision.

options.title: Fail closed plus doctor repair
options.body: Reject unsafe domains before refresh and add doctor handling that reports, rewrites, or clears unsafe legacy `enterpriseUrl` values.

options.title: Normalize at runtime
options.body: Run the existing allowlist in refresh and fall back to `github.com` for unsafe values, reducing token egress risk while leaving legacy state stored until later cleanup.

options.title: Private security workflow first
options.body: Pause public fix-shape selection and handle disclosure, migration, and release timing through the repository security process.

recommendation.title: Fail closed plus doctor repair
recommendation.body: Reject unsafe domains before refresh and add doctor handling that reports, rewrites, or clears unsafe legacy `enterpriseUrl` values.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest combined history signal across auth-profile storage, doctor migration, and Copilot OAuth hardening.
